events.text: User approved the reviewed in-process hot-swap plan and requested implementation.
Implementation started. Preserving the dirty worktree and building the ABI/load-test seam before switching the live dev path.

Implemented modular native development builds with a stable cold core, content-addressed Scene3D and Game shared libraries, frame-boundary Scene3D hot swap, exact-child restart and session replay fallback, independent caches and fingerprints, failure-safe publication, IPC observability, and cold-core import auditing. Verified live Scene3D commit, Game restart/replay, ABI tests, import audit, and a final static ReleaseFast editor ship. The architectural speedup is real, but the measured LLVM hot compiles remain 15.9 seconds for Game and 30.2 seconds for Scene3D, so the sub-five-second performance gate is explicitly still open rather than claimed complete.

resolution: Revised the native dev-module architecture to make in-process hot swap the primary adoption path, with automatic supervised process restart as the fallback. The plan keeps each old content-addressed shared object mapped until the replacement passes ABI validation, initializes, restores a host-owned versioned snapshot, switches dispatch at a frame boundary, drains GPU/background work, resets the V8 context so no callback retains old code, and then retires the old module. Load/init failures leave the old module active; quiesce, snapshot, restore, or post-commit failures trigger restart.
